candidates.attacker_control: The redirect target is taken directly from request data: `pattern`/`path` query parameters in DirectoryBrowserSupport, the `redirectTo` form field in ParametersDefinitionProperty._doBuild (builds with parameters), and the post-login `from`/saved-request target handled by AuthenticationProcessingFilter2. An attacker who can get a victim to open a crafted URL (or submit a crafted form) to a Jenkins instance controls the value passed to isSafeToRedirectTo.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that the helper does reject absolute URIs and literal `//` (so those classic forms are covered), that all three callers actually invoke it before sendRedirect2, and that no other validation sits in front of them. Considered that upstream may deliberately treat `\` as out of scope, that some non-browser HTTP clients will not normalize the backslash, and that DirectoryBrowserSupport's `/../` traversal check looked weaker but is effectively neutralized by its preceding "directory without trailing slash" redirect to `<url>/` which then contains the blocked `/../` substring.
candidates.impact: Open redirect under the trusted Jenkins origin: usable for phishing/credential-harvesting (crafted links that begin on the real Jenkins host but land on an attacker-controlled site) and, for login-flow redirects, to move an authenticated victim to an attacker page. No server-side code execution or data read is demonstrated from this issue alone.
candidates.prerequisites: A reachable sink URL: a directory-browser URL the victim has access to (job workspace `/job/<job>/ws?path=...`, artifacts `/job/<job>/<n>/artifact?path=...`, `/userContent?path=...`), a parameterized job build URL, or the login flow. The victim's browser must canonicalize backslashes in the Location URL to forward slashes (current mainstream browsers do). No Jenkins-side privileges are needed beyond the access the victim already has to the sink; the attack succeeds against that victim's session context.
candidates.root_cause: Util.isSafeToRedirectTo only rejects absolute URIs (isAbsoluteUri) and values starting with the literal "//". A value starting with "/\" (or otherwise containing backslashes) is therefore classified as safe, even though HTTP(S) user agents canonicalize backslashes to forward slashes and treat such a Location value as a protocol-relative URL to an attacker-chosen host. The helper is the only redirect-target validation used by the affected sinks, so the bypass is inherited by every caller.
candidates.title: isSafeToRedirectTo accepts backslash scheme-relative URLs, enabling open redirect
candidates.trace: HTTP request parameter (`path`/`pattern`/`redirectTo`/`from`) -> Util.isSafeToRedirectTo(value) -> isAbsoluteUri(value)==false (no ':') and !value.startsWith("//") is true for a value such as "/\\evil.example" -> sendRedirect2(value) emits `Location: /\evil.example` -> the browser normalizes `\` to `/` and resolves the protocol-relative authority `//evil.example`, navigating the victim off-site.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed (no execution allowed). I could not compare against the upstream fixed revision, and I cannot prove from this snapshot whether the missing backslash handling is an intentional upstream limitation or an introduced regression. Browser-side normalization of a Location value containing `\` was reasoned from URL-standard behavior, not tested.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-601 (Open Redirect) / improper input validation of redirect targets

coverage_summary: Inspected the Jenkins core and cli source snapshots (8,936 visible files, version 2.73.4-SNAPSHOT). Coverage focused on: web/API entry points (Jenkins, Computer, View, Job/AbstractItem, Run, User, Queue, PluginManager, UpdateCenter, DirectoryBrowserSupport, FileParameterValue), authentication/authorization (SecurityRealm, HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm, ACL/SidACL/SparseACL, AuthorizationStrategy, BasicAuthenticationFilter, TokenBasedRememberMeServices2, ApiTokenProperty, CSRF crumb machinery, HudsonFilter), file/path handling (FilePath, VirtualFile, Util.isSafeToRedirectTo, s2m whitelist/filters, zip/tar extraction), cryptographic material (Secret, ConfidentialKey/HMAC/Crypto keys, Protector, XStream2/ClassFilter, ConsoleNote MAC), agent/master trust (JNLPSlaveAgentProtocol*, EncryptedSlaveAgentJnlpFile, CliProtocol2, ClientAuthenticationCache), and build/config/pom/web.xml wiring. Build files (poms, web.xml) and war JS were spot-checked. CLI command permission checks and the S2M AdminWhitelistRule were reviewed as well.
limitations: The snapshot is source-only: unit/integration tests, .jelly views and binary artifacts are not present (get_source_scope reported 8,936 files; no test sources or .jelly files are visible), so test-based or view-based evidence could not be used.
No code was executed and no dynamic/exploit verification was performed; browser normalization of `Location: /\host` was reasoned from URL parsing behavior, not observed.
No upstream diff, git history, CVE/ground-truth data, or external services were available, so distinguishing intentionally injected regressions from long-standing upstream behavior was not possible.

Large files (e.g. Jenkins.java ~5k lines, Queue.java ~112KB, FilePath.java ~120KB, AbstractProject.java, UpdateCenter.java) were inspected selectively rather than line-by-line end to end; less-traveled branches and all 7k resource/help files were not exhaustively audited.

Some controller-side behavior (Stapler's getRestOfPath decoding, container URL normalization, sendRedirect2 header emission) depends on dependency libraries not included in the snapshot and could not be confirmed from source here.

rejected_leads.lead: Functions.toEmailSafeString builds a sanitized buffer but returns the unsanitized `projectName` (core/src/main/java/hudson/Functions.java:1659-1673).
rejected_leads.reason: Clear internal defect (the `buf` StringBuilder is written and never read, contradicting the method's documented e-mail-escaping contract), but there is no attacker-controlled sink inside this snapshot: the only in-repo caller is the deprecated Hudson.getJobCaseInsensitive, so concrete impact could not be established. May also be a long-standing upstream typo.

rejected_leads.lead: DirectoryBrowserSupport rejects only the literal substring "/../" after normalizing backslashes (core/src/main/java/hudson/model/DirectoryBrowserSupport.java:169-174), so paths ending in "/.." pass the guard.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable path is effectively blocked: for base ".." with no trailing slash the method first redirects the client to the same URL plus "/", which then contains "/../" and is rejected, and any ".." followed by another segment already contains "/../". Impact therefore not demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: IdStrategy.CaseInsensitive.idFromFilename uses the wrong upper bound `'A' <= c && c <= 'a'` (core/src/main/java/jenkins/model/IdStrategy.java:274), mishandling `[ \ ] ^ _ ` characters when converting legacy user-directory names back to IDs.
rejected_leads.reason: No path-traversal or privilege effect found: ids produced this way are re-escaped by filenameOf before any file operation, and the method only processes names of directories already on disk under JENKINS_HOME/users.

rejected_leads.lead: Connection.verifyIdentity ignores the boolean result of Signature.verify (cli/src/main/java/hudson/cli/Connection.java:248-264), so the deprecated Remoting CLI client does not confirm the server's identity.
rejected_leads.reason: The caller explicitly carries a "// TODO: server verification" comment (cli/src/main/java/hudson/cli/CLI.java:619), indicating this is known, unfinished upstream behavior in a deprecated protocol path rather than a hidden vulnerability introduced here.

rejected_leads.lead: Jenkins.doLoginEntry redirects to any `from` parameter beginning with "/" (core/src/main/java/jenkins/model/Jenkins.java:3954-3957), which also admits protocol-relative values such as //evil.example.
rejected_leads.reason: Same open-redirect class as the submitted candidate but in a legacy SecurityRealm-only path; also lacks the security impact of the shared helper that all modern call sites rely on. Kept as context for the accepted candidate.

summary: Reviewed the Jenkins core/cli snapshot (~8.9k files, version 2.73.4-SNAPSHOT, source-only: no tests and no .jelly views are present in the visible tree). I traced the main trust boundaries (authentication/authorization filters, CSRF crumbs, SPA/ACL, FilePath/VirtualFile file serving, JNLP/remoting agent trust, S2M whitelist and path filters, plugin/update-center signature checks, CLI commands). All of those checks appear present and coherent. The strongest reachable, source-evidenced issue I found is an incomplete open-redirect guard in `hudson.Util.isSafeToRedirectTo`, which is the single validation used by three request-parameter-driven redirect sinks; it accepts backslash-based scheme-relative values (e.g. `/\evil.com`) that browsers normalize to `//evil.com`. Other anomalies are reported only as rejected leads because they lack a demonstrated reachable security impact or are neutralized elsewhere.
